title: ct-migrate state snapshot
description: state/<new_ctid>.json - what the engine knew about one CT at the end of its last run. Replaced atomically on every write, so a reader never sees half a file. The append-only history in state/<new_ctid>.runs.jsonl is a stream of the 'run' object below, one per line.

schema_version.description: bumped only when a reader would break; new optional fields do not bump it

new_ctid.description: CT id on the new node - also the file name

old_ctid.description: CT id on the old node; often the same number

old_node.description: source node, as written in inventory-migrate.tsv

new_node.description: target node; required per row, never defaulted

storage.description: PVE storage id the rootfs image lives on

image.description: absolute path of the raw image, from pvesm path

image_size_gib.description: real size of the image file, rounded up. 0 means it does not exist yet

config_present.description: true once /etc/pve/lxc/<new_ctid>.conf exists on the new node. The engine writes it once and never rewrites it (G6)

config_size.description: the size= value in that config, e.g. '20G'. Empty while no config exists

size_drift.description: true when config_size disagrees with image_size_gib, which happens after an ENOSPC grow. Bookkeeping only - PVE reads the real size from the storage layer

mp_empty.description: mount point paths that were migrated as config but whose DATA was not copied. Every one of these will be an empty directory on the new node

run.description: one execution of the engine against this CT. Identical shape in 'last' and in every line of runs.jsonl

ts.description: local time the run finished, ISO 8601 with offset

epoch.description: the same instant as seconds since epoch, for sorting

lane.description: 'all' for a full run, otherwise the storage id from --storage

mode.description: 'final' means --final: the final delta off a CT that is not running. 'stopped' is the same mode under its old name - snapshots written before the rename still carry it until their next round rewrites them

status.description: 'running' is published before the transfer starts and is only ever seen live. A run killed mid-transfer is rewritten to 'interrupted' by the exit trap

reason.description: stable slug for why a run was not ok; empty when status is ok

message.description: the first ERROR / GUARD / WARN / HINT / NOTE line the run logged for this CT - the headline a human should read

rc.description: rsync exit code. -1 means the run never got that far. 0 is clean, 24 is 'files vanished' and is normal on a live CT, 11 is ENOSPC, 23 is a partial transfer and is a failure

secs.description: wall clock seconds spent in rsync, summed over ENOSPC retries

files.description: regular files transferred, summed over ENOSPC retries

literal_bytes.description: bytes rsync had to actually send as new content. The convergence metric: it should fall run over run

bytes_sent.description: total bytes put on the wire, including protocol overhead

total_bytes.description: size of the whole dataset rsync considered. A property of the CT, so it is NOT summed across retries

grow_attempts.description: how many times ENOSPC forced the image to be grown during this run
